_note: Every request the terminal scripts send themselves, beside the collector's (which are docs/endpoints/endpoints.json's, whether sent from a tab or from Node): the sign-in chain, the portal's token bootstrap and the legacy page prime of scripts/maccabi-session.mjs (npm run export -- --no-browser). Nothing here is requested by the extension. The chain is the one orenyomtov/maccabi-health documented (docs/AUTH.md there); the password road was recorded from the site's own page with scripts/discover-login.mjs. No values: what each request sends and returns is field names and shapes. test/endpoints.test.ts checks that every path written in scripts/maccabi-session.mjs is listed here.

conventions.pacing: One at a time, core.PACE_MS (300 ms) after the previous one came back, redirect hops included: the one queue in MaccabiSession.request.
conventions.auth: The login origin's /infosec calls carry Authorization: Bearer <jwt>, each with the token the previous answer handed out (originJWT from the login page, then auth -> detailsV2 -> generateV2 -> validate, or detailsV2 -> auth on the password road -> response). The portal's requests carry its session cookies; the bootstrap also Authorization: Bearer null, as the portal's own page sends it.
conventions.ended_session: A redirect from the portal to the login origin, /my.logout.php3 or /my.policy is an ended session (core.signedOutUrl, the collector's own list); a 401 or 403 from the portal is not, it is a bot challenge, passed through to the collector as a status.
conventions.attempts: One password or one code per sign-in: a refused one ends the sign-in and is never resubmitted, because repeated attempts are what lock an account. A code that is not six digits, or an empty password, is refused before anything is sent and leaves the sign-in open.

sign_in.returns: 302 to https://mac.maccabi4u.co.il/login..., followed: the login page, text/html, whose script carries originJWT = "<jwt>" and whose Set-Cookie starts the login origin's cookies
sign_in.notes: beginSignIn's first request. The originJWT is the bearer for /infosec/auth.

sign_in.sends: Authorization: Bearer <originJWT>; JSON {id: "0-<id number, no leading zeros>", password: "", type: "none"}
sign_in.returns: 200 JSON {status, jwt, message}; 4xx JSON {code} (301/304 blocked, 300/303 refused)
sign_in.notes: Starts the sign-in with the ID number. The jwt is the bearer for /infosec/otp/detailsV2.

sign_in.returns: 200 JSON {jwt, details: {allowedAge: boolean, digitalUser: boolean, phones: [{number: string (masked by the site), mobile: boolean, kosher: boolean}]}}
sign_in.notes: The member's sign-in options. Nothing is sent to the member. The jwt is the bearer for the next step on either road.
The SMS road (--sms): Maccabi texts the six-digit code to that phone. Sent once per sign-in. The jwt is the bearer for /infosec/otp/validate.

sign_in.sends: Authorization: Bearer <generateV2 jwt>; the code typed in the terminal, in the query as the site's page sends it
sign_in.returns: 200 JSON {status: "ok", jwt}; 4xx JSON {code} (303 wrong code, 302 expired)
sign_in.notes: One attempt: a refused code ends the sign-in. The jwt is the assertion, the bearer for /infosec/response.

sign_in.sends: Authorization: Bearer <detailsV2 jwt>; JSON {id: "0-<id number>", password: "<password>", type: "password"}
sign_in.notes: The password road (the default without a browser): the same endpoint as the first step, with the password, in place of generateV2 and validate. One attempt: a refused password ends the sign-in. The jwt is the assertion.

sign_in.sends: Authorization: Bearer <assertion jwt>; header relay: "home" after an SMS, "" after a password (what the site's page sends on each road)
sign_in.returns: 200 JSON {status: "ok", method: "post", destination: "https://online.maccabi4u.co.il/saml/sp/profile/post/acs", payload: {SAMLResponse: string, RelayState: string}}
sign_in.notes: The assertion as a SAML response for the portal.

sign_in.sends: application/x-www-form-urlencoded RelayState, SAMLResponse (from /infosec/response, as they came); Origin and Referer of the login origin
sign_in.returns: 303 to a portal page, followed: 200 text/html; Set-Cookie: the portal's session cookies
sign_in.notes: The portal's assertion consumer service: this is what signs the session in. Landing anywhere but the portal, or on a page that carries originJWT, is an unconfirmed session (SignInError PORTAL_SESSION_UNCONFIRMED).

session.sends: session cookies; Authorization: Bearer null; Content-Type: application/json
session.returns: 200 JSON {token: {success: boolean, content: string (the API bearer, a JWT whose claims carry mem_id and gender)}, logged_customer_info: {member_id: number, sex: string, ...}, current_customer_info: {member_id: number, ...}, session_id: string, ...}; an ended session answers with a redirect to /my.logout.php3 (SessionEndedError), as docs/endpoints/other-endpoints.json records
session.notes: The portal's own first request after landing, and the one request in this repo that returns credentials: the extension's rule against calling one (CLAUDE.md, Read-only) is the extension's, because without this there is no API token outside a tab. Sent once per sign-in (the sign-in ends with it), and once more on returning from the legacy steps, as the tab takes a fresh token on returning to /sonline/. Only token.content, logged_customer_info.member_id and sex, and session_id are kept; nothing else in the answer is read or written. A current_customer_info naming another member than logged_customer_info (a dependent selected in the portal) stops the run (DEPENDENT_SELECTED).

session.sends: session cookies, with cookie_sessionId_0_<mid> = session_id set by the script when the portal did not set it
session.returns: 200 text/html (the page; not read beyond checking it is not the login page)
session.notes: Primes the legacy /online/ services before the legacy steps, as the extension's tab does by opening the page (core.SUMMARY_PAGE): they answer only a session that has loaded one of their pages. A redirect to the login origin, /my.logout.php3 or /my.policy, or a page that carries originJWT, is an ended session.
